ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Luminous Pigment
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
DEEPFIRE_PIGMENT_MOD_1 (design/RimMandrake/deepfire_luminous_pigment_spec.md, fully ruled 2026-09-25/26). RimMandrake tier — every name here is invented, nothing is Star Wars IP (Q11a). Deepfire is a luminous pigment carried by no colour of its own: mixed with an ordinary dye it makes whatever colour the dye gives glow. It comes from crowncarpet, a rainbow bacterial mat found rarely on any ocean shore.
THE CHAIN (Phase 1, spec §2): crowncarpet (wild shore spawn on any ocean, a GenStepDef scatter at low commonality), the one-day fresh-mat clock (dies fast, dies at once if chilled — CompMatVitality), the Deepfire press (a screw press and an alchemical retort welded together, powered only, gated by a research project hidden until a mat is first seen), the refining recipe, Deepfire itself (a resource that glows faintly in a stockpile), and the GlowTank (a slow, low-yield cultured source). The whole gate can be turned to Buildable or Unbuildable instead of Research.
PAINTING (spec §3): a real designator/WorkGiver/comp mechanism coats a wall, floor, furniture, art piece, apparel or weapon in Deepfire (up to three coats; colour comes from however the target is already painted/dyed, Deepfire adds the glow). Floors cluster into shared area lights rather than one per cell. A first coat bumps an art item's quality once, or adds a flat/percentage Beauty bonus to everything else (plus a room-line bonus for coated floors). Worn apparel and equipped weapons light their wearer through one moving per-pawn proxy, with a matching darkness-targeting combat tradeoff (easier to hit at range, easier to land a melee blow, both only while genuinely glowing in the dark) — reachable from a lacquer gizmo on the pawn, or (with Ideology) a checkbox on the styling station.
STATUS (spec §4, the "purple engine"): titled and common pawns alike react to wearing or surrounding themselves in Deepfire; a titled pawn's own lit quarters and a lit public room impressing a visiting dignitary are both wired.
THE GODS (spec §5, with Ninefold loaded): every Ninefold god reacts to a first coat (building, worn item, or a tagged statue), and to a sale or gift of Deepfire goods.
CUISINE (spec §6): 14 glow-hediff families with 15 recipes on any stove and the chef-skill-steered outcome mechanism.
Every number above — the chain's costs and yields, every painting number (coat radius/intensity, per-target costs, clustering, the five paintable-target toggles, combat penalties, beauty bonuses), status thresholds and mood scale, the god deltas, and Cuisine's skill gates — is a real Mod Settings toggle or slider; turning a whole group off degrades gracefully (existing coats/thoughts keep working, nothing new is created).
The Scald's Utinni-tier sourcing (the bottom-walkers laying crowncarpet as they pass, and the Stillfluid/Thornwillow fixative recipe) is a patch in the Utinni layer, not this mod — this mod is francise-free and fully functional (wild shore spawn) with the Scald absent.
